proposed.title: Thor: Love and Thunder
proposed.text: When Gorr attacks New Asgard and takes its children, Valkyrie fights beside Thor and goes with him to Omnipotence City and the Shadow Realm to get them back. She steals Zeus's thunderbolt for him, and Gorr wounds her in the Shadow Realm.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: New Asgard's king. Joins Thor's quest to rescue the stolen children.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: An old friend who leads the quest to rescue New Asgard's children.

changes.evidence: Thor: Love and Thunder: Thor teams up with Jane, Valkyrie and Korg against Gorr at New Asgard, they travel together to Omnipotence City, Valkyrie steals Zeus's thunderbolt as they escape, and Gorr injures her in the Shadow Realm. A renewed alliance on screen with no stage.

now.title: VisionQuest#4
now.text: Ultron is a prisoner inside White Vision's mind. When he tricks Vision into giving up control of his body, he takes Tommy.
now.on_a_card_about_b: A captive mind who seizes Vision's body, then takes Tommy.
now.on_b_card_about_a: A boy Ultron takes after seizing Vision's body.

proposed.text: Ultron is a prisoner inside White Vision's mind. When Vision gives him control of his body to fight Jocasta, Ultron traps Vision inside his own mind and leaves with Tommy.

changes.evidence: VisionQuest #4 'Malware': unable to defeat Jocasta, Vision yields physical control to Ultron; Ultron then traps Vision and the AIs in the Mindspace and leaves with Tommy. Ultron tricks Jocasta, not Vision. (Kept as a connection: they share #4, and #5 shows Ultron talking with Tommy before handing him to Paladin.)

The only stage says it itself: in Thunderbolts* Valentina cites the last president's Red Hulk rampage to Congress without naming him, and they are never seen together. Ross is in Black Widow and Valentina only in its post-credits scene, with no scene between them, and she is not in Captain America: Brave New World. Knowing about someone is not a connection, and his rampage is only a talking point for her, not a huge consequence.

proposed.title: Spider-Man (1994)#22
proposed.text: In a flashback to Blade's origin, his human mother leaves him at a New Orleans orphanage after his vampire father abandons them.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: Blade's mother, who leaves him at an orphanage.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: Her half-vampire son, left at an orphanage.

changes.evidence: 'Blade, the Vampire Hunter' (#22): Whistler tells Blade's origin in a flashback. Miriam is on screen there for the first time (flashback only): she leaves Eric at a New Orleans orphanage after his vampire father, Deacon Frost, abandons them. She is shown as a photo in #23, and her return as the vampire queen comes in #48, where the current first stage sits.
